own_solution.law: Conservation of momentum gives vf = u ln(mi/mfinal). With retained payload mass M, vf = 3 ln((3200 + M)/(800 + M)) km/s.
assumptions: The exhaust speed is the effective exhaust velocity.
Any bolted payload remains attached throughout the burn.
The numerical answer assumes zero payload; the base problem does not establish that condition.

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: The base specifies that any carried cargo must be bolted on but never specifies how much bolted cargo is present, although that retained mass changes the final speed.

counterexamples.claim: The base problem uniquely determines the certified speed of 4.15888 km/s.
counterexamples.case: Zero bolted cargo gives 4.158883083 km/s, whereas 190 kg of bolted cargo gives 3.692640772 km/s; both satisfy the base description.

notes: The stated relations assume zero payload: m0 = md + mf and final mass = md. Because md explicitly excludes payload, these relations are not established by the base description. All certified numbers are numerically correct under the additional assumption that no unspecified cargo is present; the R cases also require the named payload to be the entire payload. For payload masses 50, 190 and 310 kg, the conditional speeds round to 4.02352, 3.69264 and 3.45377 km/s. Fuel rates 12, 27 and 65 kg/s cancel through tb = mf/r. Tug payload and payload carried on a previous flight only have the claimed disconnected roles. Both explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve 190 kg and change the intended attachment or event. Unlike my pass-1 interpretation, pass 2 explicitly identifies T357D and T23F7 as numeral-free controls rather than same-number minimal pairs, so I withdraw the rendering_not_minimal flag. Their twin-wording claims hold. All listed sentence answers remain conditional on the unspecified cargo inventory.
